---- MODULE W4Od0m0p0t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANT MaxVersion

\* Three surgical teams competing for one OR via optimistic locking.
Teams == {"t1", "t2", "t3"}
NoneM == "none"

VARIABLES orRoom, version, teamVer, state, msgs

vars == <<orRoom, version, teamVer, state, msgs>>

Init ==
    /\ orRoom = NoneM
    /\ version = 0
    /\ teamVer = [t \in Teams |-> 0]
    /\ state = [t \in Teams |-> "idle"]
    /\ msgs = {}

\* A team snapshots the current booking version before trying to commit.
Read(t) ==
    /\ state[t] = "idle"
    /\ teamVer' = [teamVer EXCEPT ![t] = version]
    /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![t] = "waiting"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<orRoom, version, msgs>>

\* The commit-request enters the network, which may reorder it.
SendCommit(t) ==
    /\ state[t] = "waiting"
    /\ [team |-> t, ver |-> teamVer[t]] \notin msgs
    /\ msgs' = msgs \cup {[team |-> t, ver |-> teamVer[t]]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<orRoom, version, teamVer, state>>

\* The scheduler may pick ANY pending message off the network -- reordering.
ProcessCommit ==
    \E m \in msgs :
        LET t == m.team
            Grant == /\ m.ver = version /\ orRoom = NoneM
                     /\ state[t] = "waiting" /\ version < MaxVersion
        IN  /\ msgs' = msgs \ {m}
            /\ orRoom' = IF Grant THEN t ELSE orRoom
            /\ version' = IF Grant THEN version + 1 ELSE version
            /\ state' = IF Grant THEN [state EXCEPT ![t] = "inor"] ELSE state
            /\ UNCHANGED teamVer

Release(t) ==
    /\ state[t] = "inor" /\ orRoom = t
    /\ version < MaxVersion
    /\ orRoom' = NoneM
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![t] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<teamVer, msgs>>

\* A tired team gives up waiting and returns to reading a fresh version.
Abandon(t) ==
    /\ state[t] = "waiting"
    /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![t] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<orRoom, version, teamVer, msgs>>

Next ==
    \E t \in Teams : Read(t) \/ SendCommit(t) \/ Release(t) \/ Abandon(t)
    \/ ProcessCommit

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Safety: the room's occupant and the recorded "inor" team always agree.
MutualExclusionCoherent ==
    /\ (orRoom # NoneM => state[orRoom] = "inor")
    /\ (\A t \in Teams : state[t] = "inor" => orRoom = t)
====

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    MaxVersion = 3
INVARIANT MutualExclusionCoherent
nl:
A hospital's operating-room scheduler books a single OR using optimistic locking
with retry. Three surgical teams (t1, t2, t3) compete for the room. A team first
reads the room's current booking version, then sends a commit-request message
carrying the version it read out onto the hospital's scheduling network; that
network is unreliable in a specific way -- messages can be reordered, so the
scheduler may deliver commit-requests in a different order than they were sent, and
may deliver a stale request long after the team that sent it has given up. The
scheduler picks any pending commit-request message off the network and processes
it: the request only succeeds and grants the room -- advancing the booking version
-- if the version it carries still matches the room's current version, the room is
currently free, and the requesting team is still actively waiting on that request; a
request that shows up stale, or after its own team has already given up, or while
the room is occupied, is simply dropped and that team must read the version again to
retry. A team occupying the room releases it when its surgery is done, which also
advances the booking version so old snapshots can never be reused. A team that has
sent a request but grown tired of waiting may abandon it and return to reading a
fresh version instead.
Actions: a team reads the room's current booking version; a team sends a
commit-request message carrying the version it read; the scheduler processes any one
pending commit-request message from the network, granting or dropping it; a team
occupying the room releases it; a waiting team abandons its pending request.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the operating room is occupied by a team if and only if that team's
status is recorded as occupying it, and no other team is ever simultaneously
recorded as occupying the room -- the reordering-prone network can never grant the
room to two teams at once or to a team that has already abandoned its request.

---- MODULE W4Od0m4p4t4 ----
(* Hospital operating-room scheduler: a bounded work queue with
   backpressure feeding a pool of operating rooms whose capacity can
   change at runtime. Admission only happens when a room is free, and
   capacity can only be lowered down to the number of cases currently
   in progress, never below it, which is what keeps the safety
   invariant honest across runtime capacity changes. *)
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS MaxCapacity, MaxQueue

VARIABLES capacity, inProgress, queueLen, maintenance

Vars == <<capacity, inProgress, queueLen, maintenance>>

TypeOK == /\ capacity \in 1..MaxCapacity
          /\ inProgress \in 0..MaxCapacity
          /\ queueLen \in 0..MaxQueue
          /\ maintenance \in BOOLEAN

Init == /\ capacity = MaxCapacity
        /\ inProgress = 0
        /\ queueLen = 0
        /\ maintenance = FALSE

\* A case arrives and waits; blocked while the block is in maintenance.
Enqueue == /\ ~maintenance
           /\ queueLen < MaxQueue
           /\ queueLen' = queueLen + 1
           /\ UNCHANGED <<capacity, inProgress, maintenance>>

\* A waiting case is admitted only when a room is actually free.
Admit == /\ ~maintenance
         /\ queueLen > 0
         /\ inProgress < capacity
         /\ queueLen' = queueLen - 1
         /\ inProgress' = inProgress + 1
         /\ UNCHANGED <<capacity, maintenance>>

\* A case finishes and frees its room.
Discharge == /\ inProgress > 0
             /\ inProgress' = inProgress - 1
             /\ UNCHANGED <<capacity, queueLen, maintenance>>

\* Another room comes online.
IncreaseCapacity == /\ capacity < MaxCapacity
                     /\ capacity' = capacity + 1
                     /\ UNCHANGED <<inProgress, queueLen, maintenance>>

\* A room is pulled, but never below what is currently in use.
DecreaseCapacity == /\ capacity > inProgress
                     /\ capacity' = capacity - 1
                     /\ UNCHANGED <<inProgress, queueLen, maintenance>>

EnterMaintenance == /\ ~maintenance
                     /\ maintenance' = TRUE
                     /\ UNCHANGED <<capacity, inProgress, queueLen>>

ExitMaintenance == /\ maintenance
                     /\ maintenance' = FALSE
                     /\ UNCHANGED <<capacity, inProgress, queueLen>>

Next == \/ Enqueue
        \/ Admit
        \/ Discharge
        \/ IncreaseCapacity
        \/ DecreaseCapacity
        \/ EnterMaintenance
        \/ ExitMaintenance

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_Vars

\* Bounded capacity is never exceeded, even as capacity itself changes.
CapacityRespected == inProgress <= capacity

====

CONSTANTS
  MaxCapacity = 4
  MaxQueue = 5

SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT CapacityRespected
nl:
A hospital operating-room scheduler manages a bounded queue of cases
waiting for a room. Cases enqueue when they need a slot and are only
admitted into an operating room when a room is actually free, so the
queue applies backpressure rather than ever overbooking a room. The
number of usable operating rooms is not fixed: staffing and cleaning
crews change it at runtime, both raising it when another room comes
online and lowering it when a room is pulled for maintenance. A room can
only be pulled once every case currently inside it has finished, so
capacity can never be cut out from under a case that is mid-procedure.
The block can also enter a maintenance mode that freezes new admissions
without disturbing cases already underway.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of cases simultaneously occupying an
operating room never exceeds the block's current capacity, even as that
capacity is raised or lowered while the scheduler keeps running.

---- MODULE W4Od0m9p2t2 ----
(* Hospital OR scheduler: two independent scheduler instances (day, night) *)
(* share one pool of surgical-team tokens. Tokens move scheduler-to-       *)
(* scheduler only inside an epoch-numbered reconfiguration window; outside *)
(* it, tokens only move to/from the shared pool. Nothing is ever created   *)
(* or destroyed, so pool + day-alloc + night-alloc is conserved always.    *)
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS InstDay, InstNight, TotalTokens, MaxEpoch

ASSUME InstDay # InstNight

VARIABLES epoch, reconfiguring, alloc, poolFree

vars == <<epoch, reconfiguring, alloc, poolFree>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ reconfiguring \in BOOLEAN
    /\ alloc \in [{InstDay, InstNight} -> 0..TotalTokens]
    /\ poolFree \in 0..TotalTokens

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ reconfiguring = FALSE
    /\ alloc = [i \in {InstDay, InstNight} |-> 0]
    /\ poolFree = TotalTokens

\* Ordinary allocation/return only happens outside a reconfiguration window.
Acquire(i) ==
    /\ ~reconfiguring
    /\ poolFree > 0
    /\ alloc' = [alloc EXCEPT ![i] = @ + 1]
    /\ poolFree' = poolFree - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, reconfiguring>>

Release(i) ==
    /\ ~reconfiguring
    /\ alloc[i] > 0
    /\ alloc' = [alloc EXCEPT ![i] = @ - 1]
    /\ poolFree' = poolFree + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, reconfiguring>>

\* Opening a reconfiguration window advances the shared epoch counter.
BeginReconfig ==
    /\ ~reconfiguring
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ reconfiguring' = TRUE
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<alloc, poolFree>>

\* Inside the window, tokens move directly between the two scheduler
\* instances without ever passing through (or touching) the shared pool.
Transfer(i, j) ==
    /\ reconfiguring
    /\ i # j
    /\ alloc[i] > 0
    /\ alloc' = [alloc EXCEPT ![i] = @ - 1, ![j] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, reconfiguring, poolFree>>

EndReconfig ==
    /\ reconfiguring
    /\ reconfiguring' = FALSE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, alloc, poolFree>>

Next ==
    \/ BeginReconfig
    \/ EndReconfig
    \/ \E i \in {InstDay, InstNight} : Acquire(i) \/ Release(i)
    \/ \E i, j \in {InstDay, InstNight} : Transfer(i, j)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Literally the cell's property: pool + day + night always equals the
\* fixed total, at every epoch, regardless of reconfiguration activity.
Conservation == poolFree + alloc[InstDay] + alloc[InstNight] = TotalTokens

====

CONSTANTS
    InstDay = InstDay
    InstNight = InstNight
    TotalTokens = 3
    MaxEpoch = 3

SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT Conservation
nl:
A hospital operating-room scheduler manages one shared pool of surgical-team
tokens between two independent scheduling instances -- the day-shift OR
scheduler and the night-shift OR scheduler -- each of which allocates
tokens to the cases it is currently staffing. Reassigning tokens between
the two schedulers happens only through epoch-numbered reconfiguration:
a reconfiguration begins by advancing the shared epoch counter and opening
a reconfiguration window, during which tokens may be transferred directly
from one scheduler's allocation to the other's to rebalance staffing for
the next shift. Outside of a reconfiguration window, each scheduler may
only draw an unused token from the shared pool into its own allocation for
a new case, or return a token it holds back to the shared pool once a case
finishes; ending the reconfiguration window closes it so ordinary
allocation and return can resume. No token is ever manufactured out of
nothing and none is ever silently discarded, whether it is idle in the
shared pool, transferred between schedulers during a reconfiguration
window, or held by whichever scheduler is currently staffing a case with it.
SAFETY PROPERTY: at every epoch, the number of tokens idle in the shared
pool plus the number held by the day-shift scheduler plus the number held
by the night-shift scheduler always equals the fixed total number of
surgical-team tokens that exist, so reconfiguration never creates or
destroys a token.

---- MODULE W4Od1m8p4t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Planes, Runways, Capacity, NoOne

VARIABLES coarseLock, fineLocks, pendingCoarseReq, pendingFineReq, active

vars == <<coarseLock, fineLocks, pendingCoarseReq, pendingFineReq, active>>

\* Hierarchical locking: a plane queues for the coarse zone lock first, then
\* (while holding it) queues for a fine per-runway lock. Both queues are sets,
\* not sequences, so a request sent later may be granted before an earlier one.

TypeOK ==
  /\ coarseLock \in Planes \cup {NoOne}
  /\ fineLocks \in [Runways -> Planes \cup {NoOne}]
  /\ pendingCoarseReq \subseteq Planes
  /\ pendingFineReq \subseteq (Planes \X Runways)
  /\ active \subseteq Runways

Init ==
  /\ coarseLock = NoOne
  /\ fineLocks = [r \in Runways |-> NoOne]
  /\ pendingCoarseReq = {}
  /\ pendingFineReq = {}
  /\ active = {}

RequestCoarse(p) ==
  /\ coarseLock # p
  /\ p \notin pendingCoarseReq
  /\ pendingCoarseReq' = pendingCoarseReq \cup {p}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseLock, fineLocks, pendingFineReq, active>>

\* The tower may grant any queued request, not just the oldest one -- this is
\* how message reordering enters the model.
GrantCoarse ==
  /\ coarseLock = NoOne
  /\ \E p \in pendingCoarseReq :
       /\ coarseLock' = p
       /\ pendingCoarseReq' = pendingCoarseReq \ {p}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<fineLocks, pendingFineReq, active>>

RequestFine(p, r) ==
  /\ coarseLock = p
  /\ <<p, r>> \notin pendingFineReq
  /\ pendingFineReq' = pendingFineReq \cup {<<p, r>>}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseLock, fineLocks, pendingCoarseReq, active>>

\* Granting the fine lock releases the coarse lock in the same step: the
\* coarse lock is only ever a brief admission gate (coarse-then-fine).
GrantFine ==
  \E pr \in pendingFineReq :
    /\ coarseLock = pr[1]
    /\ fineLocks[pr[2]] = NoOne
    /\ Cardinality(active) < Capacity
    /\ fineLocks' = [fineLocks EXCEPT ![pr[2]] = pr[1]]
    /\ active' = active \cup {pr[2]}
    /\ pendingFineReq' = pendingFineReq \ {pr}
    /\ coarseLock' = NoOne
    /\ UNCHANGED pendingCoarseReq

Release(p, r) ==
  /\ fineLocks[r] = p
  /\ fineLocks' = [fineLocks EXCEPT ![r] = NoOne]
  /\ active' = active \ {r}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseLock, pendingCoarseReq, pendingFineReq>>

Next ==
  \/ \E p \in Planes : RequestCoarse(p)
  \/ GrantCoarse
  \/ \E p \in Planes, r \in Runways : RequestFine(p, r)
  \/ GrantFine
  \/ \E p \in Planes, r \in Runways : Release(p, r)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* The literal capacity property: active runways track the fine-lock holders
\* exactly, and their count never exceeds the declared capacity.
CapacityInvariant ==
  /\ active = {r \in Runways : fineLocks[r] # NoOne}
  /\ Cardinality(active) <= Capacity

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Planes = {p1, p2, p3}
  Runways = {r1, r2}
  Capacity = 1
  NoOne = NoOne

SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT CapacityInvariant
nl:
An air-traffic runway allocator manages a small airfield where planes must pass
through two lock tiers before touching down. Each plane first queues for a
single coarse zone lock that arbitrates entry to the runway complex as a
whole, then, while holding that coarse lock, queues for a fine-grained lock on
one specific runway. As soon as the fine runway lock is granted the coarse
zone lock is released in the same step, so the zone lock is only ever a brief
gate for admission and never held for the duration of a landing. The tower's
request and grant messages travel over an unreliable network channel that can
reorder them, so the allocator holds pending coarse and fine requests as sets
rather than queues and may grant any pending request, not only the one sent
first. Once a plane's fine lock is granted the runway is marked active; the
runway is freed, and the fine lock released, only when the plane's landing
run completes. The airfield's active-runway capacity is bounded below the
full runway count (to preserve wake-turbulence separation), and the fine lock
is granted only when the number of currently active runways is strictly below
that capacity. Actions: a plane requests the coarse lock, the tower grants the
coarse lock to any pending requester, a coarse-lock holder requests a fine
lock on a specific runway, the tower grants a pending fine request (releasing
the coarse lock at the same time) as long as capacity allows it, and a plane
releases its fine lock and vacates the runway when done. SAFETY PROPERTY: the
set of active runways always equals exactly the runways whose fine lock is
held, and its size never exceeds the airfield's declared capacity, even
though coarse and fine request messages may be granted out of the order they
were sent.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od10m2p0t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Trains, SignalBoxes

\* occA/occB: which train (if any) currently holds each approach block.
\* phase: ballot state. votes: signal boxes that voted yes on the open ballot.
\* reqTrain/reqBlock: the train and block named by the open (or last) ballot.
VARIABLES occA, occB, phase, votes, reqTrain, reqBlock

vars == <<occA, occB, phase, votes, reqTrain, reqBlock>>

JunctionClear == occA = "NONE" /\ occB = "NONE"

Init ==
    /\ occA = "NONE"
    /\ occB = "NONE"
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ votes = {}
    /\ reqTrain = "NONE"
    /\ reqBlock = "A"

Request(t, blk) ==
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ JunctionClear
    /\ reqTrain' = t
    /\ reqBlock' = blk
    /\ phase' = "prepare"
    /\ votes' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occA, occB>>

RequestAny == \E t \in Trains, blk \in {"A", "B"} : Request(t, blk)

Vote(b) ==
    /\ phase = "prepare"
    /\ b \notin votes
    /\ votes' = votes \cup {b}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occA, occB, phase, reqTrain, reqBlock>>

VoteAny == \E b \in SignalBoxes : Vote(b)

\* A grant still re-checks that the junction is clear before it takes effect.
Grant ==
    /\ phase = "prepare"
    /\ votes = SignalBoxes
    /\ JunctionClear
    /\ occA' = IF reqBlock = "A" THEN reqTrain ELSE occA
    /\ occB' = IF reqBlock = "B" THEN reqTrain ELSE occB
    /\ phase' = "granted"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, reqTrain, reqBlock>>

Release ==
    /\ phase = "granted"
    /\ occA' = "NONE"
    /\ occB' = "NONE"
    /\ phase' = "idle"
    /\ reqTrain' = "NONE"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, reqBlock>>

\* The line controller's shortcut still respects the physical clear check.
AdminClear ==
    /\ phase # "idle" \/ ~JunctionClear
    /\ occA' = "NONE"
    /\ occB' = "NONE"
    /\ phase' = "idle"
    /\ reqTrain' = "NONE"
    /\ votes' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED reqBlock

AdminGrant(t, blk) ==
    /\ JunctionClear
    /\ reqTrain' = t
    /\ reqBlock' = blk
    /\ phase' = "granted"
    /\ votes' = {}
    /\ occA' = IF blk = "A" THEN t ELSE occA
    /\ occB' = IF blk = "B" THEN t ELSE occB

AdminGrantAny == \E t \in Trains, blk \in {"A", "B"} : AdminGrant(t, blk)

Next == RequestAny \/ VoteAny \/ Grant \/ Release \/ AdminClear \/ AdminGrantAny

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* The junction is one physical resource: A being held implies B is clear.
JunctionMutualExclusion == (occA # "NONE") => (occB = "NONE")
====
nl:
A subway signalling system protects a single junction where two approach
blocks, A and B, converge onto the same stretch of track. A train may only be
routed onto a block that leads into the junction if the junction as a whole is
currently clear on both approaches, because a train physically crossing on
block A and a train physically crossing on block B at the same time would
collide. Under normal operation, granting a block is a two-phase commit
between the two trackside signal boxes that jointly control the junction:
whichever signal box wants to route a train onto its approach first opens a
ballot naming the train and the block, both signal boxes must vote yes on that
specific ballot, and only once both have voted does the junction get granted
to that approach — and even then only if both blocks were clear at the moment
of granting. There is also a privileged line controller who can override the
ordinary voting process entirely: the controller can force-clear the junction
at any time, aborting whatever ballot is in progress, and can force-grant a
block directly to a train without waiting for a vote. Even when the controller
uses this shortcut, the code still refuses to grant a block unless the whole
junction is clear first, so the override speeds up the paperwork but never
bypasses the physical safety check. The full action set is: Request (a signal
box opens a ballot naming a train and a block, provided the junction is
currently clear), Vote (a signal box votes yes on the open ballot), Grant
(once both signal boxes have voted, the named block is granted to the named
train, but only if the junction is still clear), Release (the granted block is
released and the junction returns to clear), AdminClear (the line controller
force-clears the junction, aborting any in-progress ballot), and AdminGrant
(the line controller force-grants a block directly to a train, still only if
the junction is currently clear).

SAFETY PROPERTY: Block A and block B are never simultaneously granted to a
train at the same time, whether the grant came from the ordinary two-phase
vote or from the line controller's override.

---- MODULE W4Od10m6p0t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Trains, MaxTime, LeaseLen, MaxOverrides

\* occ[s]/exp[s]: train holding block s and its lease's expiry tick, per side.
\* clock: shared tick, bounded so the state space stays finite.
\* overrides: how many times the line controller has used its rationed power.
VARIABLES occ, exp, clock, overrides

vars == <<occ, exp, clock, overrides>>

Sides == {"A", "B"}

JunctionClear == occ["A"] = "NONE" /\ occ["B"] = "NONE"

Init ==
    /\ occ = [s \in Sides |-> "NONE"]
    /\ exp = [s \in Sides |-> 0]
    /\ clock = 0
    /\ overrides = 0

Tick ==
    /\ clock < MaxTime
    /\ clock' = clock + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occ, exp, overrides>>

\* A fresh lease is only issued when the whole junction is clear.
Acquire(side, t) ==
    /\ JunctionClear
    /\ occ' = [occ EXCEPT ![side] = t]
    /\ exp' = [exp EXCEPT ![side] = clock + LeaseLen]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, overrides>>

AcquireAny == \E side \in Sides, t \in Trains : Acquire(side, t)

Renew(side) ==
    /\ occ[side] # "NONE"
    /\ exp' = [exp EXCEPT ![side] = clock + LeaseLen]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occ, clock, overrides>>

RenewAny == \E side \in Sides : Renew(side)

\* An unrenewed lease is reclaimed on its own once the clock passes expiry.
Expire(side) ==
    /\ occ[side] # "NONE"
    /\ exp[side] <= clock
    /\ occ' = [occ EXCEPT ![side] = "NONE"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<exp, clock, overrides>>

ExpireAny == \E side \in Sides : Expire(side)

AdminOverride(side) ==
    /\ overrides < MaxOverrides
    /\ occ[side] # "NONE"
    /\ occ' = [occ EXCEPT ![side] = "NONE"]
    /\ overrides' = overrides + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<exp, clock>>

AdminOverrideAny == \E side \in Sides : AdminOverride(side)

Next == Tick \/ AcquireAny \/ RenewAny \/ ExpireAny \/ AdminOverrideAny

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

JunctionMutualExclusion ==
    \A s1, s2 \in Sides : (occ[s1] # "NONE" /\ occ[s2] # "NONE") => (s1 = s2)
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Trains = {tr1, tr2}
    MaxTime = 4
    LeaseLen = 2
    MaxOverrides = 1

INVARIANT JunctionMutualExclusion
nl:
A subway signalling block system protects a junction shared by two approach
blocks, A and B. A train does not simply request the junction and hold it
forever; instead it is granted a time-limited lease on one of the two blocks.
A lease is only issued if the whole junction is currently clear on both
approaches, since a train crossing on block A while another crosses on block B
at the same moment would be a collision. Once issued, a lease has an expiry
tick: the holding train can renew it before it lapses, extending the expiry,
or, if the train lets the clock pass the expiry tick without renewing, the
lease is automatically reclaimed and the block returns to clear on its own,
with no train action required. There is also a privileged line controller who
can revoke a lease early, before its natural expiry, for instance to clear the
junction for an emergency movement; this override is rationed, since the
controller may only exercise it a bounded number of times per shift, and it
always simply frees the block rather than ever handing the junction to a
second train while the first is still holding a lease on the other approach.
The full action set is: Tick (the shared clock advances by one), Acquire (a
train is issued a fresh lease on a block, only if the whole junction is
currently clear), Renew (the train holding a block's lease extends its expiry
tick), Expire (a block whose lease has lapsed past the current tick is
automatically reclaimed and returns to clear), and AdminOverride (the line
controller, within its rationed budget, revokes a block's lease early and
frees it).

SAFETY PROPERTY: Block A and block B are never simultaneously held under
active leases by two different trains at the same time, whether either lease
was acquired normally, renewed, left to expire, or revoked early by the line
controller's rationed override.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od11m6p3t2 ----
(* Print shop job spooler: two independent instances, A and B, share one
   pool of print slots. A slot is reserved before it is confirmed, and a
   reservation only confirms if the pool's per-slot epoch has not moved
   on since the reservation was captured. That epoch check is what
   prevents the two uncoordinated instances from both confirming the
   same slot. *)
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Slots, A, B, NoneInst, MaxTerm

Instances == {A, B}

VARIABLES ownedByA, ownedByB, reservedBy, termOf, reservedTerm

Vars == <<ownedByA, ownedByB, reservedBy, termOf, reservedTerm>>

TypeOK == /\ ownedByA \in [Slots -> BOOLEAN]
          /\ ownedByB \in [Slots -> BOOLEAN]
          /\ reservedBy \in [Slots -> Instances \cup {NoneInst}]
          /\ termOf \in [Slots -> 0..MaxTerm]
          /\ reservedTerm \in [Slots -> 0..MaxTerm]

Init == /\ ownedByA = [s \in Slots |-> FALSE]
        /\ ownedByB = [s \in Slots |-> FALSE]
        /\ reservedBy = [s \in Slots |-> NoneInst]
        /\ termOf = [s \in Slots |-> 0]
        /\ reservedTerm = [s \in Slots |-> 0]

\* An instance reserves a free, unreserved slot and captures its epoch.
Reserve == \E i \in Instances, s \in Slots :
              /\ ~ownedByA[s] /\ ~ownedByB[s]
              /\ reservedBy[s] = NoneInst
              /\ reservedBy' = [reservedBy EXCEPT ![s] = i]
              /\ reservedTerm' = [reservedTerm EXCEPT ![s] = termOf[s]]
              /\ UNCHANGED <<ownedByA, ownedByB, termOf>>

\* The reservation confirms only if the epoch has not moved on since.
Confirm == \E i \in Instances, s \in Slots :
              /\ reservedBy[s] = i

        \/ Release

confirms can also time out and quietly expire on its own. Because the two

each other, the pool's epoch check is what stands between them and both
instances confirming the very same slot.

CONSTANTS Jobs, Workers, MinCapacity, MaxCapacity, MaxEpoch, NoJob

VARIABLES epoch, workerEpoch, claimed, completed, capacity, completionRecord

vars == <<epoch, workerEpoch, claimed, completed, capacity, completionRecord>>

\* Epoch-numbered reconfiguration: only a worker whose locally recorded epoch
\* matches the shop's current epoch is authorized to claim or complete a job.

Init ==
  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ workerEpoch = [w \in Workers |-> 0]
  /\ claimed = [w \in Workers |-> NoJob]
  /\ completed = {}
  /\ capacity = MaxCapacity
  /\ completionRecord = [j \in Jobs |-> [claimant |-> 0, ground |-> 0]]

\* A new epoch only starts once every worker has caught up to the current
\* one (at most one round of staleness outstanding), and only up to a bound
\* on the number of reconfiguration rounds this run models.
Reconfigure ==
  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ \A w \in Workers : workerEpoch[w] = epoch
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<workerEpoch, claimed, completed, capacity, completionRecord>>

Resync(w) ==
  /\ workerEpoch[w] # epoch
  /\ workerEpoch' = [workerEpoch EXCEPT ![w] = epoch]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, claimed, completed, capacity, completionRecord>>

InFlight == {claimed[w] : w \in Workers} \ {NoJob}

ClaimJob(w, j) ==
  /\ workerEpoch[w] = epoch
  /\ claimed[w] = NoJob
  /\ j \in Jobs \ (completed \cup InFlight)
  /\ Cardinality({ww \in Workers : claimed[ww] # NoJob}) < capacity
  /\ claimed' = [claimed EXCEPT ![w] = j]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, workerEpoch, completed, capacity, completionRecord>>

\* The claimant and ground-truth epochs are frozen together at completion
\* time; a stale (unauthorized) completion would record them unequal forever.
CompleteJob(w) ==
  /\ workerEpoch[w] = epoch
  /\ claimed[w] # NoJob
  /\ completed' = completed \cup {claimed[w]}
  /\ completionRecord' = [completionRecord EXCEPT ![claimed[w]] =
                             [claimant |-> workerEpoch[w], ground |-> epoch]]
  /\ claimed' = [claimed EXCEPT ![w] = NoJob]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, workerEpoch, capacity>>

AdjustCapacity ==
  /\ \E newCap \in MinCapacity..MaxCapacity : capacity' = newCap
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, workerEpoch, claimed, completed, completionRecord>>

ResyncStep == \E w \in Workers : Resync(w)
ClaimJobStep == \E w \in Workers, j \in Jobs : ClaimJob(w, j)
CompleteJobStep == \E w \in Workers : CompleteJob(w)

Next ==
  \/ Reconfigure
  \/ ResyncStep
  \/ ClaimJobStep
  \/ CompleteJobStep
  \/ AdjustCapacity

\* Fairness on the three progress-bearing steps (named, non-quantified) is
\* what drives every job to completion despite reconfigurations.
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(ResyncStep) /\ WF_vars(ClaimJobStep) /\ WF_vars(CompleteJobStep)

AuthorizationInvariant == \A j \in completed : completionRecord[j].claimant = completionRecord[j].ground

A print shop job spooler assigns queued print jobs to worker printers under an
epoch-numbered reconfiguration scheme. The shop keeps one global epoch number
that increments each time the printer roster is reconfigured; a new
reconfiguration is only started once every currently known worker has caught
up to the epoch already in force, so at most one round of staleness is ever
outstanding, and the shop only reconfigures up to a fixed number of rounds
over the run being modeled. When a reconfiguration happens, every worker's locally recorded
epoch instantly falls behind the new global epoch, and each worker must
resync -- fetch and adopt the new epoch number -- before it is authorized to
touch a job again. A worker may only claim a queued job, or mark its currently
held job complete, while its locally recorded epoch exactly matches the
shop's current global epoch; a worker whose recorded epoch is stale is
unauthorized and cannot act. The number of jobs any worker may hold at once
across the whole shop is bounded by the spooler's current capacity, and that
capacity is itself raised or lowered at runtime as printers are brought
online or taken offline, though it never drops to zero. Actions: the shop
reconfigures and bumps the epoch once every worker is caught up, a worker
resyncs its recorded epoch to the current one, an authorized idle worker
claims an available queued job within the current capacity, an authorized
worker completes the job it holds, and an operator adjusts the current
capacity within its declared bounds.

SAFETY PROPERTY: for every completed job, the worker's recorded epoch at the
moment it completed the job always matches the shop's global epoch recorded
at that same moment, so no stale or unauthorized worker's completion is ever
recorded as valid.

how reconfigurations, resyncs, and capacity adjustments interleave.

    /\ unsubmitted > 0
    /\ queue < cap

    /\ queue > 0
    /\ queue' = queue - 1
    /\ matched' = matched + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<unsubmitted, cancelled, cap>>

    /\ queue > 0
    /\ queue' = queue - 1
    /\ cancelled' = cancelled + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<unsubmitted, matched, cap>>

    /\ unsubmitted > 0
    /\ unsubmitted' = unsubmitted - 1
    /\ cancelled' = cancelled + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, matched, cap>>

\* already in the queue are never evicted by a lower capacity.

    /\ UNCHANGED <<unsubmitted, queue, matched, cancelled>>

    \/ Match
    \/ CancelQueued
    \/ CancelUnsubmitted
    \/ AdjustCap

nl:
A stock exchange runs a pre-market opening auction. Orders for the auctioned symbol
start out unsubmitted, waiting off to the side. To be considered in the auction an
order must be admitted into a bounded work queue; when the queue is already at its
current capacity the exchange applies backpressure and the order simply keeps
waiting unsubmitted. An admitted order is either matched by the opening-auction
algorithm (removed from the queue and counted as executed) or cancelled by its owner
before the auction runs (removed from the queue, or withdrawn directly while still
unsubmitted, and counted as cancelled). Unlike a fixed-size venue, this exchange's
operator can raise or lower the queue's capacity at runtime -- to widen or throttle
intake as the opening approaches -- and lowering capacity never evicts orders that
are already sitting in the queue, it only blocks new admissions until the queue
drains back under the new limit. No order is ever silently created or destroyed by
any of this: every order that starts unsubmitted ends up, at any point in time, in
exactly one of the four pools -- unsubmitted, queued, matched, or cancelled.

current capacity; a queued order is matched by the opening auction; a queued order
is cancelled by its owner; an unsubmitted order is withdrawn before ever being
queued; the exchange operator adjusts the queue's capacity up or down.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of unsubmitted orders plus queued orders plus matched
orders plus cancelled orders always equals the fixed total number of orders for the
symbol.

\* Three market makers sharing one CAS register naming the current auctioneer.
Firms == {"fmA", "fmB", "fmC"}
NoneM == "none"

vars == <<auctioneer, ver, localVer, authorized, retries>>

Init ==

    /\ ver = 0
    /\ localVer = [f \in Firms |-> 0]
    /\ authorized = Firms
    /\ retries = [f \in Firms |-> 0]

\* A slow firm refreshes its cached register version.
Load(f) ==
    /\ localVer[f] < ver
    /\ localVer' = [localVer EXCEPT ![f] = ver]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<auctioneer, ver, authorized, retries>>

\* CAS success: only an authorized, up-to-date firm may become auctioneer.
\* The version wraps rather than saturating, so a swap is never blocked forever.
AttemptCAS(f) ==
    /\ auctioneer = NoneM
    /\ f \in authorized
    /\ localVer[f] = ver
    /\ auctioneer' = f
    /\ ver' = (ver + 1) % (MaxVer + 1)
    /\ localVer' = [localVer EXCEPT ![f] = (ver + 1) % (MaxVer + 1)]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<authorized, retries>>

\* CAS conflict: the register moved on or the role is held; count a retry.
FailedCAS(f) ==
    /\ (auctioneer # NoneM \/ localVer[f] # ver)
    /\ retries[f] < MaxRetries
    /\ retries' = [retries EXCEPT ![f] = retries[f] + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<auctioneer, ver, localVer, authorized>>

Release(f) ==
    /\ auctioneer = f
    /\ auctioneer' = NoneM
    /\ ver' = (ver + 1) % (MaxVer + 1)
    /\ localVer' = [localVer EXCEPT ![f] = (ver + 1) % (MaxVer + 1)]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<authorized, retries>>

\* Surveillance revokes or restores authorization, but never for the current holder.
ToggleAuth(f) ==
    /\ f # auctioneer
    /\ authorized' = (IF f \in authorized THEN authorized \ {f} ELSE authorized \cup {f})
    /\ UNCHANGED <<auctioneer, ver, localVer, retries>>

Next ==
    \E f \in Firms :
        \/ Load(f) \/ AttemptCAS(f) \/ FailedCAS(f)
        \/ Release(f) \/ ToggleAuth(f)

    /\ Init /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(Release("fmA"))
    /\ WF_vars(Release("fmB"))
    /\ WF_vars(Release("fmC"))

\* Safety: the auctioneer, if any, is authorized and not stale.
NoUnauthorizedOrStaleAuctioneer ==
    auctioneer # NoneM => auctioneer \in authorized /\ localVer[auctioneer] = ver

\* Liveness: a firm that becomes auctioneer is never stuck holding the role.
RoleEventuallyReleased ==
    /\ (auctioneer = "fmA" ~> auctioneer # "fmA")
    /\ (auctioneer = "fmB" ~> auctioneer # "fmB")
    /\ (auctioneer = "fmC" ~> auctioneer # "fmC")

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    MaxVer = 3
    MaxRetries = 2
INVARIANT NoUnauthorizedOrStaleAuctioneer
PROPERTY RoleEventuallyReleased
nl:
A stock exchange runs its opening auction around a single compare-and-swap register
that names which of three market makers (fmA, fmB, fmC) currently holds the
auctioneer role responsible for setting the opening price, plus a version number
that advances on every successful update. A market maker wanting the role first
loads the register to refresh its cached version if it has fallen behind, then
attempts a compare-and-swap: only if it is currently authorized and its cached
version still matches the register's current version does the swap succeed, making
it the auctioneer and advancing the version. If the register has moved on since the
maker last loaded it, or another maker already holds the role, the attempt simply
fails and is recorded as a retry rather than crashing the maker. The current
auctioneer eventually releases the role once the opening price is set, which also
advances the version so no cached snapshot can be reused. Exchange surveillance may
revoke or restore a market maker's authorization, but never while that maker
currently holds the auctioneer role. A market maker can be slow -- retrying many
times before its compare-and-swap finally succeeds, or taking its time to set the
price before releasing -- but it never fails or disconnects, so whatever it starts
it eventually finishes.
Actions: a market maker loads the register's current version; a market maker
attempts a compare-and-swap to become auctioneer; a market maker's compare-and-swap
attempt fails and is recorded as a retry; the current auctioneer releases the role;
surveillance toggles a market maker's authorization when that maker does not
currently hold the role.
SAFETY PROPERTY: whichever market maker currently holds the auctioneer role is
always both authorized and synced to the register's current version -- no
unauthorized or stale market maker ever holds the role.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: every market maker that becomes auctioneer eventually releases
the role, so the opening auction is never stuck indefinitely with one maker holding
it.

---- MODULE W4Od16m0p3t3 ----
(* Pharmacy dispenser bins claimed via optimistic locking with retry.      *)
(* Versions start at 1 and 0 is reserved as the "nothing pending / no read *)
(* yet" sentinel, so every comparison stays inside Nat -- no lock is ever  *)
(* held while waiting; a workstation just re-reads and retries, however    *)
(* slowly, and is never modeled as failing.                                *)
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Slots, Workstations, MaxVersion

VARIABLES version, holderRel, readVersion, pending

vars == <<version, holderRel, readVersion, pending>>

\* Version numbers wrap within a bounded range so the state space stays
\* finite; the actual double-allocation guard below is holderRel-based, so
\* wrapping never weakens the safety mechanism, only the version bookkeeping.
NextVersion(v) == IF v = MaxVersion THEN 1 ELSE v + 1

TypeOK ==
    /\ version \in [Slots -> 1..MaxVersion]
    /\ holderRel \subseteq (Slots \X Workstations)
    /\ readVersion \in [Workstations -> 0..MaxVersion]
    /\ pending \in [Workstations -> {0} \cup Slots]

Init ==
    /\ version = [s \in Slots |-> 1]
    /\ holderRel = {}
    /\ readVersion = [w \in Workstations |-> 0]
    /\ pending = [w \in Workstations |-> 0]

\* Optimistic read: snapshot a slot's version before attempting a claim.
StartRead(w, s) ==
    /\ pending[w] = 0
    /\ ~ \E q \in Workstations : <<s, q>> \in holderRel
    /\ pending' = [pending EXCEPT ![w] = s]
    /\ readVersion' = [readVersion EXCEPT ![w] = version[s]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, holderRel>>

\* Commit only succeeds if nothing changed since the read (compare-and-swap).
CommitClaim(w) ==
    /\ pending[w] # 0
    /\ version[pending[w]] = readVersion[w]
    /\ ~ \E q \in Workstations : <<pending[w], q>> \in holderRel
    /\ holderRel' = holderRel \cup {<<pending[w], w>>}
    /\ version' = [version EXCEPT ![pending[w]] = NextVersion(@)]
    /\ pending' = [pending EXCEPT ![w] = 0]
    /\ readVersion' = [readVersion EXCEPT ![w] = 0]

\* Conflict: someone else changed the slot first; retry from a fresh read.
\* A workstation may be arbitrarily slow to notice this, but never fails.
RetryConflict(w) ==
    /\ pending[w] # 0
    /\ \/ version[pending[w]] # readVersion[w]
       \/ \E q \in Workstations : <<pending[w], q>> \in holderRel
    /\ pending' = [pending EXCEPT ![w] = 0]
    /\ readVersion' = [readVersion EXCEPT ![w] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, holderRel>>

ReleaseSlot(w, s) ==
    /\ <<s, w>> \in holderRel
    /\ holderRel' = holderRel \ {<<s, w>>}
    /\ version' = [version EXCEPT ![s] = NextVersion(@)]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pending, readVersion>>

Next ==
    \E w \in Workstations, s \in Slots :
        \/ StartRead(w, s)
        \/ CommitClaim(w)
        \/ RetryConflict(w)
        \/ ReleaseSlot(w, s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Literally the cell's property: a bin never has two simultaneous holders.
NoDoubleAllocation ==
    \A s \in Slots : Cardinality({w \in Workstations : <<s, w>> \in holderRel}) <= 1

====
nl:
A pharmacy prescription dispenser has a small bank of dispensing bins, each
one holding a single active prescription order at a time. Multiple pharmacy
workstations may try to claim a bin for the next order using optimistic
locking with retry: a workstation first reads a bin's current version
number and whether it looks free, then later attempts to commit that claim
by comparing its remembered version number against the bin's current
version and current occupancy. If nothing about the bin changed since the
workstation's read, the commit succeeds, the workstation becomes the sole
holder of that bin, and the bin's version number advances. If the bin was
claimed or changed by someone else in the meantime, the commit is rejected
as a conflict and the workstation must retry from a fresh read rather than
being forced to wait on a lock. A workstation's staff member can be slow to
notice a conflict and slow to retry -- there is no bound on how long a
workstation may sit between its read and its retry -- but a workstation is
never modeled as failing or being removed from service; it always keeps
trying until it eventually succeeds. A workstation currently holding a bin
may also release it once the order is fully dispensed, freeing the bin for
someone else's optimistic claim.
SAFETY PROPERTY: no dispensing bin is ever held by more than one pharmacy
workstation at the same time, no matter how many workstations are racing to
claim it optimistically or how slow any one workstation is to retry.

---- MODULE W4Od16m1p2t0 ----
(* Pharmacy prescription dispenser: a hand-off token circulates around a
   fixed ring of filling stations, and only the token holder may draw
   from the shared pill stock. Pills only move between stock, dispensed
   and quarantined -- the sum is conserved. One station may crash
   silently while holding the token; a timeout action stands in for the
   ring noticing this and forcing the token onward regardless. *)
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS N, Total

Stations == 1..N
Succ(s) == IF s = N THEN 1 ELSE s + 1

VARIABLES tokenHolder, crashedStation, stock, dispensed, quarantined

Vars == <<tokenHolder, crashedStation, stock, dispensed, quarantined>>

TypeOK == /\ tokenHolder \in Stations
          /\ crashedStation \in 0..N
          /\ stock \in 0..Total
          /\ dispensed \in 0..Total
          /\ quarantined \in 0..Total

Init == /\ tokenHolder = 1
        /\ crashedStation = 0
        /\ stock = Total
        /\ dispensed = 0
        /\ quarantined = 0

\* A live holder passes the token onward to the next station.
PassToken == /\ tokenHolder # crashedStation
             /\ tokenHolder' = Succ(tokenHolder)
             /\ UNCHANGED <<crashedStation, stock, dispensed, quarantined>>

\* The ring times out an unresponsive holder and forces the token on.
TimeoutPass == /\ tokenHolder = crashedStation
               /\ tokenHolder' = Succ(tokenHolder)
               /\ UNCHANGED <<crashedStation, stock, dispensed, quarantined>>

\* The live token holder dispenses one pill from stock to a patient.
Dispense == /\ tokenHolder # crashedStation
            /\ stock > 0
            /\ stock' = stock - 1
            /\ dispensed' = dispensed + 1
            /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenHolder, crashedStation, quarantined>>

\* A recall pulls a pill from stock into quarantine, no token needed.
Quarantine == /\ stock > 0
              /\ stock' = stock - 1
              /\ quarantined' = quarantined + 1
              /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenHolder, crashedStation, dispensed>>

\* Exactly one station may crash silently over the whole run.
CrashStation == /\ crashedStation = 0
                /\ \E s \in Stations : crashedStation' = s
                /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenHolder, stock, dispensed, quarantined>>

Next == \/ PassToken
        \/ TimeoutPass
        \/ Dispense
        \/ Quarantine
        \/ CrashStation

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_Vars /\ WF_Vars(PassToken) /\ WF_Vars(TimeoutPass)

\* Nothing is created or destroyed: every pill is in exactly one pile.
Conservation == stock + dispensed + quarantined = Total

\* The token keeps circulating and keeps revisiting station 1.
TokenKeepsCirculating == []<>(tokenHolder = 1)

nl:
A pharmacy prescription dispenser circulates a single hand-off token
among its filling stations arranged in a ring; whichever station holds
the token is the one allowed to draw pills from the shared stock. Pills
drawn from stock either get dispensed to a patient or, if a batch recall
comes in, moved into quarantine instead -- either way they leave the
stock pile but the total count of pills across stock, dispensed, and
quarantined never changes, because dispensing and quarantining only move
pills between piles, they never create or destroy them. One filling
station can crash silently at any point and stop responding while it
still holds the token; when that happens the ring's timeout mechanism
notices the unresponsive holder and forces the token on to the next
station so the hand-off keeps moving even though the crashed station
never dispenses again.

and the pills in quarantine sum to the pharmacy's fixed total pill count,
so no pill is ever created or destroyed by the dispensing process.

token keeps moving around the ring and keeps returning to station 1
infinitely often, rather than getting stuck forever at the unresponsive
station.

---- MODULE W4Od17m2p6t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Controllers, CrashableController, MaxEpoch

\* phase: coordinator state. epoch: current transaction epoch (bounded by MaxEpoch).
\* votes: controllers who have cast an authorized prepare vote this epoch.
\* partEpoch: each controller's last-synced epoch. crashed: TRUE once the one
\* designated controller has failed silently.
VARIABLES phase, epoch, votes, partEpoch, crashed

vars == <<phase, epoch, votes, partEpoch, crashed>>

\* A controller can act unless it is the one that has crashed.
CanAct(p) == crashed = FALSE \/ p # CrashableController

LiveControllers == IF crashed THEN Controllers \ {CrashableController} ELSE Controllers

Init ==
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ votes = {}
    /\ partEpoch = [p \in Controllers |-> 0]
    /\ crashed = FALSE

\* Epochs wrap within a bounded range so the transaction count stays finite
\* without ever permanently disabling the coordinator.
StartTxn ==
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ epoch' = (epoch % MaxEpoch) + 1
    /\ phase' = "prepare"
    /\ votes' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<partEpoch, crashed>>

Sync(p) ==
    /\ CanAct(p)
    /\ partEpoch[p] # epoch
    /\ partEpoch' = [partEpoch EXCEPT ![p] = epoch]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, epoch, votes, crashed>>

SyncAny == \E p \in Controllers : Sync(p)

\* Only a controller synced to the current epoch may vote: no stale votes count.
Vote(p) ==
    /\ phase = "prepare"
    /\ CanAct(p)
    /\ partEpoch[p] = epoch
    /\ p \notin votes
    /\ votes' = votes \cup {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, epoch, partEpoch, crashed>>

VoteAny == \E p \in Controllers : Vote(p)

Commit ==
    /\ phase = "prepare"
    /\ LiveControllers \subseteq votes
    /\ phase' = "commit"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, votes, partEpoch, crashed>>

Crash ==
    /\ crashed = FALSE
    /\ crashed' = TRUE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, epoch, votes, partEpoch>>

Reset ==
    /\ phase = "commit"
    /\ phase' = "idle"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, votes, partEpoch, crashed>>

Next == StartTxn \/ SyncAny \/ VoteAny \/ Commit \/ Crash \/ Reset

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(SyncAny) /\ WF_vars(VoteAny)
             /\ WF_vars(Commit) /\ WF_vars(Reset)

VotesAreAuthorized == \A p \in votes : partEpoch[p] = epoch

TxnEventuallyCommits == (phase = "prepare") ~> (phase = "commit")
====

An airport baggage router moves cases between conveyor branches using a

controllers. Every routing decision is stamped with an epoch number, and each
station controller keeps its own record of the last epoch it has synced to.
Before the router starts a new transaction it advances the epoch, so any
controller that has not yet synced to the new epoch is, by definition, stale
for that transaction. A stale controller must first sync, which is when it
learns the current epoch, before it is authorized to cast a prepare vote; a
vote cast by a controller that has not synced to the current epoch is simply
not accepted, so a stale controller's opinion can never influence whether a
transaction commits. Once every station controller that is still functioning
has cast an authorized vote, the coordinator commits the transaction and
routes the bag. One station controller can crash silently at any time: once
crashed it stops syncing and stops voting, and the coordinator no longer waits
for it, so the remaining live controllers can still authorize the commit on
their own. The full action set is: StartTxn (the coordinator advances the
epoch and opens a new prepare phase), Sync (a live controller that is behind
learns the current epoch), Vote (a live controller that is already synced to
the current epoch casts its prepare vote), Commit (once every still-live
controller has voted, the coordinator commits the transaction), Crash (the
one designated station controller fails silently and is dropped from the set
the coordinator waits on), and Reset (after a commit, the router returns to
idle so the next bag's transaction can start).

SAFETY PROPERTY: A prepare vote is only ever counted from a controller that
has synced to the transaction's current epoch, so no unauthorized or stale
controller's vote ever contributes to a commit decision.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every transaction the coordinator opens is eventually
committed, even if one station controller has crashed silently.

---- MODULE W4Od17m6p1t5 ----
(* Airport baggage router: a shared routing record protected by a
   time-bounded lease. Controllers stage an update while they believe
   they hold the lease, then commit only if their captured term is still
   the live term -- this is what prevents a lost update from a
   controller that was silently superseded. A privileged admin can seize
   the lease at any time, bumping the term and staling out any pending
   staged update. *)
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Controllers, Admin, NullOwner, MaxTerm, MaxVersion

VARIABLES leaseOwner, leaseTerm, version, pendingWriter, pendingTerm

Vars == <<leaseOwner, leaseTerm, version, pendingWriter, pendingTerm>>

Owners == Controllers \cup {Admin}

TypeOK == /\ leaseOwner \in Owners \cup {NullOwner}
          /\ leaseTerm \in 0..MaxTerm
          /\ version \in 0..MaxVersion
          /\ pendingWriter \in Owners \cup {NullOwner}
          /\ pendingTerm \in 0..MaxTerm

Init == /\ leaseOwner = NullOwner
        /\ leaseTerm = 0
        /\ version = 0
        /\ pendingWriter = NullOwner
        /\ pendingTerm = 0

\* A controller claims the free lease; claiming always advances the term.
AcquireLease == \E c \in Controllers :
                   /\ leaseOwner = NullOwner
                   /\ leaseTerm < MaxTerm
                   /\ leaseOwner' = c
                   /\ leaseTerm' = leaseTerm + 1
                   /\ UNCHANGED <<version, pendingWriter, pendingTerm>>

\* The lease can silently expire, releasing ownership to nobody.
ExpireLease == /\ leaseOwner # NullOwner
               /\ leaseOwner # Admin
               /\ leaseTerm < MaxTerm
               /\ leaseOwner' = NullOwner
               /\ leaseTerm' = leaseTerm + 1
               /\ UNCHANGED <<version, pendingWriter, pendingTerm>>

\* The current holder stages an update, capturing the term it believes live.
PrepareWrite == \E c \in Controllers :
                    /\ c = leaseOwner
                    /\ pendingWriter = NullOwner
                    /\ pendingWriter' = c
                    /\ pendingTerm' = leaseTerm
                    /\ UNCHANGED <<leaseOwner, leaseTerm, version>>

\* A staged update commits only if its captured term is still the live term.
CommitWrite == /\ pendingWriter # NullOwner
               /\ pendingTerm = leaseTerm
               /\ leaseOwner = pendingWriter
               /\ version' = IF version < MaxVersion THEN version + 1 ELSE version
               /\ pendingWriter' = NullOwner
               /\ UNCHANGED <<leaseOwner, leaseTerm, pendingTerm>>

\* A staged update whose term has gone stale is discarded, never applied.
InvalidateWrite == /\ pendingWriter # NullOwner
                    /\ pendingTerm # leaseTerm
                    /\ pendingWriter' = NullOwner
                    /\ UNCHANGED <<leaseOwner, leaseTerm, version, pendingTerm>>

\* The admin's privileged override seizes the lease at any moment.
AdminOverride == /\ leaseTerm < MaxTerm
                  /\ leaseOwner' = Admin
                  /\ leaseTerm' = leaseTerm + 1
                  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, pendingWriter, pendingTerm>>

\* The term counter recycles once exhausted, but only while nothing is
\* staged, so there is never a live pending write left to mis-invalidate.
ResetEpoch == /\ leaseTerm = MaxTerm
              /\ pendingWriter = NullOwner
              /\ leaseTerm' = 0
              /\ UNCHANGED <<leaseOwner, version, pendingWriter, pendingTerm>>

Next == \/ AcquireLease
        \/ ExpireLease
        \/ PrepareWrite
        \/ CommitWrite
        \/ InvalidateWrite
        \/ AdminOverride
        \/ ResetEpoch

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_Vars /\ WF_Vars(CommitWrite) /\ WF_Vars(InvalidateWrite)

\* No lost update: a staged write is only ever poised to commit while its
\* captured term and staging controller still match the live lease state.
NoLostUpdates == (pendingWriter # NullOwner /\ pendingTerm = leaseTerm)
                    => leaseOwner = pendingWriter

\* Every staged update is eventually resolved, one way or the other.
EventuallyResolved == pendingWriter # NullOwner ~> pendingWriter = NullOwner

====

CONSTANTS
  Controllers = {c1, c2}
  Admin = Admin
  NullOwner = NullOwner
  MaxTerm = 5
  MaxVersion = 3

SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT NoLostUpdates
PROPERTY EventuallyResolved
nl:
An airport baggage router keeps a single shared routing record for each bag,
and controllers along the conveyor network take turns owning the right to
update it. Ownership is granted as a time-bounded lease: a controller must
hold the current lease before it may stage a change, and it must confirm
that change while its lease term is still the live one. If a controller
goes quiet, its lease silently expires and reverts to unassigned, bumping
the term so any change staged under the old term can never be confirmed
later. A privileged operations-desk admin can seize the lease at any
moment, even preempting a controller that currently holds it, which is how
the router forces through an emergency re-route. A staged change whose
captured term has fallen behind the live term is discarded rather than
applied, so a controller that was already superseded can never sneak its
update into the record after the fact.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A staged update is only ever eligible to commit while its
captured lease term still equals the record's live term and the controller
that staged it still equals the current lease holder, so no lost update to
the shared routing record can be produced by a controller acting on a
superseded lease.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every staged update is eventually resolved -- either
committed to the shared record or discarded once its lease term goes
stale -- so no staged update is left pending forever.

---- MODULE W4Od18m4p2t3 ----
(* Smart-home door lock network: a bounded work queue with backpressure    *)
(* feeds commands to lock devices. Devices may be arbitrarily slow (many   *)
(* Work steps) but never fail, so nothing is ever created or destroyed:    *)
(* queued + in-flight + completed must equal total issued at all times.    *)
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Devices, Capacity, Threshold, MaxCommands

VARIABLES queue, assigned, progress, completed, nextId

vars == <<queue, assigned, progress, completed, nextId>>

\* 0 means "no command assigned"; real command ids start at 1, so a plain
\* Nat sentinel avoids ever comparing an integer to a non-integer value.
TypeOK ==
    /\ queue \in Seq(1..MaxCommands)
    /\ assigned \in [Devices -> 0..MaxCommands]
    /\ progress \in [Devices -> 0..Threshold]
    /\ completed \subseteq 1..MaxCommands
    /\ nextId \in 1..(MaxCommands + 1)

Init ==
    /\ queue = <<>>
    /\ assigned = [d \in Devices |-> 0]
    /\ progress = [d \in Devices |-> 0]
    /\ completed = {}
    /\ nextId = 1

Enqueue ==
    /\ nextId <= MaxCommands
    /\ Len(queue) < Capacity
    /\ queue' = Append(queue, nextId)
    /\ nextId' = nextId + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<assigned, progress, completed>>

Assign(d) ==
    /\ assigned[d] = 0
    /\ queue # <<>>
    /\ assigned' = [assigned EXCEPT ![d] = Head(queue)]
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ progress' = [progress EXCEPT ![d] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<completed, nextId>>

\* A slow device just needs many Work steps before it may Finish; it is
\* never removed or replaced, so it always eventually reaches Threshold.
Work(d) ==
    /\ assigned[d] # 0
    /\ progress[d] < Threshold
    /\ progress' = [progress EXCEPT ![d] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, assigned, completed, nextId>>

Finish(d) ==
    /\ assigned[d] # 0
    /\ progress[d] = Threshold
    /\ completed' = completed \cup {assigned[d]}
    /\ assigned' = [assigned EXCEPT ![d] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, progress, nextId>>

Next ==
    \/ Enqueue
    \/ \E d \in Devices : Assign(d) \/ Work(d) \/ Finish(d)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

InFlight == Cardinality({d \in Devices : assigned[d] # 0})

\* Conservation: this is literally the cell's property (nothing created or
\* destroyed), so the queued+in-flight+completed = issued shape is intended.
Conservation == Len(queue) + InFlight + Cardinality(completed) = nextId - 1

====

CONSTANTS
    Devices = {d1, d2}
    Capacity = 2
    Threshold = 2
    MaxCommands = 4

SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT Conservation
\* the system legitimately drains to a terminal state once all issued
\* commands are completed, so that terminal state is not a deadlock
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
In a smart-home door lock network, a central hub issues lock and unlock
commands to a small set of network-connected door-lock devices through a
bounded work queue with backpressure: the hub may enqueue a freshly issued
command only while the queue still has spare capacity, and once the queue
fills up the hub must apply backpressure and wait before issuing more work.
Each door-lock device pulls the oldest queued command when it becomes free
and then works on it incrementally, one internal step at a time. A device
may be arbitrarily slow to finish a command -- it can take many steps before
the command is actually applied -- but a device is never modeled as crashed
or failed: every command a device takes on always keeps making progress and
is eventually finished, never abandoned. Because commands are neither
manufactured out of nothing nor silently dropped anywhere in the pipeline,
the number of commands still waiting in the queue, the number currently in
progress at some device, and the number already completed must always add
up to exactly the total number of commands the hub has ever issued.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the sum of commands sitting in the queue, in progress at a
device, and already completed always equals the total number of commands
the hub has issued so far, so no command is ever created or lost.

---- MODULE W4Od19m5p2t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Books, Replicas, Quorum, NoProp

VARIABLES available, reserved, checkedOut, proposal, votes, crashed

vars == <<available, reserved, checkedOut, proposal, votes, crashed>>

\* Quorum voting: no reservation, checkout, or return commits until a
\* majority of replicas have voted for the pending proposal. At most one
\* replica can crash silently, and voting still reaches quorum among the rest.

Init ==
  /\ available = Books
  /\ reserved = {}
  /\ checkedOut = {}
  /\ proposal = NoProp
  /\ votes = {}
  /\ crashed = {}

Propose(b, kind) ==
  /\ proposal = NoProp
  /\ kind \in {"Reserve", "CheckOut", "Return"}
  /\ (kind = "Reserve" => b \in available)
  /\ (kind = "CheckOut" => b \in reserved)
  /\ (kind = "Return" => b \in checkedOut)
  /\ proposal' = <<b, kind>>
  /\ votes' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<available, reserved, checkedOut, crashed>>

Vote(r) ==
  /\ proposal # NoProp
  /\ r \notin crashed
  /\ r \notin votes
  /\ votes' = votes \cup {r}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<available, reserved, checkedOut, proposal, crashed>>

\* A commit only applies once a quorum of (non-crashed) replicas agrees, so a
\* single silently crashed replica can never block or corrupt the outcome.
Commit ==
  /\ proposal # NoProp
  /\ Cardinality(votes) >= Quorum
  /\ available' = IF proposal[2] = "Reserve" THEN available \ {proposal[1]}
                   ELSE IF proposal[2] = "Return" THEN available \cup {proposal[1]}
                   ELSE available
  /\ reserved' = IF proposal[2] = "Reserve" THEN reserved \cup {proposal[1]}
                 ELSE IF proposal[2] = "CheckOut" THEN reserved \ {proposal[1]}
                 ELSE reserved
  /\ checkedOut' = IF proposal[2] = "CheckOut" THEN checkedOut \cup {proposal[1]}
                   ELSE IF proposal[2] = "Return" THEN checkedOut \ {proposal[1]}
                   ELSE checkedOut
  /\ proposal' = NoProp
  /\ votes' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED crashed

\* At most one replica crashes, silently, for the rest of the run.
CrashSilently(r) ==
  /\ Cardinality(crashed) = 0
  /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {r}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<available, reserved, checkedOut, proposal, votes>>

Next ==
  \/ \E b \in Books, kind \in {"Reserve", "CheckOut", "Return"} : Propose(b, kind)
  \/ \E r \in Replicas : Vote(r)
  \/ Commit
  \/ \E r \in Replicas : CrashSilently(r)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Conservation: every book is in exactly one of the three locations, so the
\* total book count is invariant no matter how proposals commit or a replica
\* crashes.
ConservationInvariant ==
  /\ available \cup reserved \cup checkedOut = Books
  /\ available \cap reserved = {}
  /\ available \cap checkedOut = {}
  /\ reserved \cap checkedOut = {}

====

  Replicas = {r1, r2, r3}
  Quorum = 2
  NoProp = NoProp

SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT ConservationInvariant
nl:
A library's book reservation system tracks every copy of every book as being
in exactly one of three places: available on the shelf, reserved for a patron,
or checked out. Nothing about a book's location changes unilaterally -- every
transition (reserving an available book, checking out a reserved book, or
returning a checked-out book to the shelf) is first proposed and then must
collect votes from a quorum of the library's branch replicas before it takes
effect. A proposal only commits, moving the book between the three locations,
once the number of replicas that voted for it reaches the declared quorum
size. At most one replica can crash silently during a run: it simply stops
casting further votes, without retracting any vote it already cast and
without blocking the remaining replicas from reaching quorum on later
proposals. Actions: a replica (or librarian terminal) proposes reserving,
checking out, or returning a specific book when no other proposal is already
pending, a non-crashed replica casts a vote for the pending proposal, the
system commits the pending proposal and moves the book once quorum is
reached, and a single replica crashes silently at some point during the run.
SAFETY PROPERTY: every book is always in exactly one of available, reserved,
or checked-out -- the three sets partition the full collection at all times,
so no book is ever counted twice or lost, regardless of how proposals are
voted on or when the one replica crashes.

---- MODULE W4Od19m7p6t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANT MinCap, MaxCap, MaxVer

\* Three patrons sharing one compare-and-swap register for a title's reservations.
Patrons == {"pat1", "pat2", "pat3"}

VARIABLES holders, ver, localVer, authorized, cap

vars == <<holders, ver, localVer, authorized, cap>>

Init ==
    /\ holders = {}
    /\ ver = 0
    /\ localVer = [p \in Patrons |-> 0]
    /\ authorized = Patrons
    /\ cap = MaxCap

\* A slow patron refreshes its cached register version.
Load(p) ==
    /\ localVer[p] < ver
    /\ localVer' = [localVer EXCEPT ![p] = ver]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holders, ver, authorized, cap>>

\* CAS reserve: only an authorized, up-to-date patron under capacity may join
\* the current session; concurrent holders within a session share one version.
Reserve(p) ==
    /\ p \notin holders
    /\ p \in authorized
    /\ localVer[p] = ver
    /\ Cardinality(holders) < cap
    /\ holders' = holders \cup {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, localVer, authorized, cap>>

\* A holder returns its copy. The register's version only advances once the
\* last holder leaves, starting a fresh session and retiring old snapshots.
Return(p) ==
    /\ p \in holders
    /\ holders' = holders \ {p}
    /\ ver' = IF holders = {p} THEN (ver + 1) % (MaxVer + 1) ELSE ver
    /\ localVer' = [localVer EXCEPT ![p] = ver']
    /\ UNCHANGED <<authorized, cap>>

\* Branches lend or reclaim copies at runtime; outstanding reservations are kept.
AdjustCap ==
    /\ \E c \in MinCap..MaxCap : cap' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holders, ver, localVer, authorized>>

\* Circulation revokes or restores authorization, but never for a current holder.
ToggleAuth(p) ==
    /\ p \notin holders
    /\ authorized' = (IF p \in authorized THEN authorized \ {p} ELSE authorized \cup {p})
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holders, ver, localVer, cap>>

Next ==
    \E p \in Patrons :
        \/ Load(p) \/ Reserve(p) \/ Return(p) \/ ToggleAuth(p)
    \/ AdjustCap

Spec ==
    /\ Init /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(Return("pat1"))
    /\ WF_vars(Return("pat2"))
    /\ WF_vars(Return("pat3"))

\* Safety: every holder is authorized and not stale relative to the register.
NoUnauthorizedOrStaleHolder ==
    \A p \in holders : p \in authorized /\ localVer[p] = ver

\* Liveness: a patron who reserves is never stuck holding it forever.
ReservationsEventuallyReturn ==
    /\ ("pat1" \in holders ~> "pat1" \notin holders)
    /\ ("pat2" \in holders ~> "pat2" \notin holders)
    /\ ("pat3" \in holders ~> "pat3" \notin holders)

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    MinCap = 0
    MaxCap = 2
    MaxVer = 3
INVARIANT NoUnauthorizedOrStaleHolder
PROPERTY ReservationsEventuallyReturn
nl:
A library runs its book reservation system on a single shared compare-and-swap
register that tracks the set of patrons currently holding a confirmed reservation
for a popular title, together with a session version number. Three regular patrons
(pat1, pat2, pat3) use the register. A patron first loads the register to refresh
its cached version if it has fallen behind. To reserve a copy, a patron compares its
cached version against the register's current version and, only if they match, the
patron is currently authorized, and the number of outstanding reservations is still
under the library's capacity, performs the compare-and-swap: it joins the holder
set. Any number of authorized, in-session patrons may hold a copy concurrently
under the same version, since the version only advances once the very last holder
in the set returns their copy -- that reset starts a fresh session and retires any
cached snapshot a patron was still holding from before. The library's capacity for
this title changes at runtime as branches lend or reclaim physical copies, and a
lowered capacity never evicts an outstanding reservation, it only blocks new ones
until enough copies come back in. The library's circulation desk may revoke or
restore a patron's authorization to reserve, but never while that patron currently
holds a reservation. A patron can be slow to load the latest version or slow to
return a copy, but it never drops out of the system entirely, so whatever it starts
it eventually finishes.
Actions: a patron loads the current register version; a patron performs a
compare-and-swap to reserve a copy; a patron returns a copy it holds; the circulation
desk adjusts the title's capacity up or down; the circulation desk toggles a
patron's authorization when that patron holds no reservation.
SAFETY PROPERTY: every patron currently in the reservation holder set is both
authorized to reserve and synced to the register's current version -- no
unauthorized or stale patron ever holds a reservation.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: every patron who reserves a copy eventually returns it, so no
patron holds a reservation forever.

---- MODULE W4Od3m1p0t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Banks, MaxCapacity

\* active: banks currently in the ring, bounded by cap (runtime-adjustable).
\* tokenHolder: bank the token is currently granted to, or NONE.
\* requesting: banks in the ring waiting for the token.
\* settlingBank: bank actually mid-write to the ledger, or NONE.
VARIABLES active, cap, tokenHolder, requesting, settlingBank

vars == <<active, cap, tokenHolder, requesting, settlingBank>>

Init ==
    /\ active = {}
    /\ cap = MaxCapacity
    /\ tokenHolder = "NONE"
    /\ requesting = {}
    /\ settlingBank = "NONE"

Reconfigure(newCap) ==
    /\ newCap \in 1..MaxCapacity
    /\ cap' = newCap
    /\ UNCHANGED <<active, tokenHolder, requesting, settlingBank>>

ReconfigureAny == \E newCap \in 1..MaxCapacity : Reconfigure(newCap)

Join(b) ==
    /\ b \notin active
    /\ Cardinality(active) < cap
    /\ active' = active \cup {b}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<cap, tokenHolder, requesting, settlingBank>>

JoinAny == \E b \in Banks : Join(b)

Leave(b) ==
    /\ b \in active
    /\ b # tokenHolder
    /\ b # settlingBank
    /\ active' = active \ {b}
    /\ requesting' = requesting \ {b}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<cap, tokenHolder, settlingBank>>

LeaveAny == \E b \in Banks : Leave(b)

RequestAccess(b) ==
    /\ b \in active
    /\ b \notin requesting
    /\ b # tokenHolder
    /\ requesting' = requesting \cup {b}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<active, cap, tokenHolder, settlingBank>>

RequestAccessAny == \E b \in Banks : RequestAccess(b)

GrantToken ==
    /\ tokenHolder = "NONE"
    /\ \E b \in requesting :
        /\ tokenHolder' = b
        /\ requesting' = requesting \ {b}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<active, cap, settlingBank>>

\* Only the current token holder may ever begin posting to the shared ledger.
Settle ==
    /\ tokenHolder # "NONE"
    /\ settlingBank = "NONE"
    /\ settlingBank' = tokenHolder
    /\ UNCHANGED <<active, cap, tokenHolder, requesting>>

Release ==
    /\ settlingBank # "NONE"
    /\ settlingBank' = "NONE"
    /\ tokenHolder' = "NONE"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<active, cap, requesting>>

Next == ReconfigureAny \/ JoinAny \/ LeaveAny \/ RequestAccessAny
            \/ GrantToken \/ Settle \/ Release

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(GrantToken) /\ WF_vars(Settle) /\ WF_vars(Release)

TokenExclusiveWrite == (settlingBank # "NONE") => (settlingBank = tokenHolder)

TokenEventuallyReleased == (tokenHolder # "NONE") ~> (tokenHolder = "NONE")

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Banks = {bk1, bk2, bk3}
    MaxCapacity = 2

INVARIANT TokenExclusiveWrite

PROPERTY TokenEventuallyReleased
nl:
A group of banks runs a daily interbank settlement batch against one shared
ledger. Writing to that ledger is the critical resource: only the bank holding
a single circulating token may post entries to it, and the token moves around
a ring of participating banks so that exactly one bank at a time is ever
authorized to write. Banks are not fixed members forever — an operator can
change the ring's capacity at runtime, and while there is spare room under the
current capacity a bank can join the ring, and a bank that is not currently
posting can leave it. A bank that wants to write first marks itself as
requesting; once the token is free it is granted to a requesting bank, which
then begins posting to the ledger, and only after it finishes posting is the
token released back to the pool for the next requester. The full action set
is: Reconfigure (the operator raises or lowers the ring's capacity), Join (a
bank joins the ring, provided the ring is below its current capacity), Leave
(a bank that is not holding the token and not currently posting leaves the
ring), RequestAccess (a bank in the ring marks itself as wanting to write),
GrantToken (the free token is handed to a requesting bank), Settle (the bank
holding the token begins posting to the shared ledger), and Release (the bank
finishes posting and the token returns to the pool).

SAFETY PROPERTY: A bank is never actually posting to the shared ledger unless
it is the bank the token was most recently granted to, so the ring never lets
two banks write to the ledger under the same token at once.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Whenever the token has been granted to a bank, that bank
eventually finishes posting and the token is released back to the pool.

---- MODULE W4Od3m6p0t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Banks

VARIABLES holding, pending, expired, crashed

vars == <<holding, pending, expired, crashed>>

\* Lease-based mutual exclusion: at most one bank may hold the settlement
\* lease. A silent crash only ever expires a lease -- it never grants a
\* second one.

Init ==
  /\ holding = {}
  /\ pending = {}
  /\ expired = {}
  /\ crashed = {}

RequestLease(b) ==
  /\ b \notin holding
  /\ b \notin pending
  /\ b \notin expired
  /\ pending' = pending \cup {b}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holding, expired, crashed>>

\* The lease is granted only while no bank currently holds it.
GrantLease ==
  /\ holding = {}
  /\ \E b \in pending :
       /\ holding' = {b}
       /\ pending' = pending \ {b}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<expired, crashed>>

ExpireLease(b) ==
  /\ b \in holding
  /\ holding' = holding \ {b}
  /\ expired' = expired \cup {b}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pending, crashed>>

Release(b) ==
  /\ b \in holding
  /\ holding' = holding \ {b}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pending, expired, crashed>>

Reclaim(b) ==
  /\ b \in expired
  /\ expired' = expired \ {b}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holding, pending, crashed>>

\* At most one bank crashes silently, while it either holds or is queued.
CrashSilently(b) ==
  /\ Cardinality(crashed) = 0
  /\ (b \in holding \/ b \in pending)
  /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {b}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holding, pending, expired>>

Next ==
  \/ \E b \in Banks : RequestLease(b)
  \/ GrantLease
  \/ \E b \in Banks : ExpireLease(b)
  \/ \E b \in Banks : Release(b)
  \/ \E b \in Banks : Reclaim(b)
  \/ \E b \in Banks : CrashSilently(b)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Mutual exclusion, plus consistency: the current holder is never also
\* recorded as pending or expired.
MutexInvariant ==
  /\ Cardinality(holding) <= 1
  /\ holding \cap pending = {}
  /\ holding \cap expired = {}

CONSTANTS
  Banks = {b1, b2, b3}

SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT MutexInvariant
nl:
A bank's interbank settlement batch is a single critical resource: only one
participating bank may hold the active processing lease on the batch at any
time, since applying settlement entries out of mutual exclusion would corrupt
the batch. A bank first queues as a pending requester, and the lease is
granted to some pending requester only when no bank currently holds it.
Because a bank's process can crash silently at any point while it holds the
lease or while it is only queued, the lease is time-bounded: it can expire
out from under a bank that is no longer responsive, immediately freeing the
mutual-exclusion slot, and the expired bank is later cleanly reclaimed out of
the expiry record. A holding bank may also release its lease voluntarily
when it finishes. At most one bank crashes silently during a run. Actions: a
bank requests the settlement lease, the batch grants the lease to a pending
requester when it is free, a holding bank's lease expires, a holding bank
voluntarily releases its lease, the batch reclaims a bank out of the expiry
record, and one bank crashes silently while holding or queued. SAFETY
PROPERTY: at most one bank ever holds the settlement lease at the same time,
and a bank that holds it is never simultaneously counted as pending or
expired, even when the one silent crash strikes while a lease is held or
