EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANT MaxEpoch

\* Three settlement banks; hierarchical locking: a coarse batch lock, then a fine leg lock.
Banks == {"bA", "bB", "bC"}
NoneP == "none"

VARIABLES coarse, fine, epoch, localEpoch, authorized

vars == <<coarse, fine, epoch, localEpoch, authorized>>

Init ==
    /\ coarse = NoneP
    /\ fine = NoneP
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ localEpoch = [b \in Banks |-> 0]
    /\ authorized = Banks

\* A slow bank catches its cached epoch up to the current one.
Sync(b) ==
    /\ localEpoch[b] < epoch
    /\ localEpoch' = [localEpoch EXCEPT ![b] = epoch]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, fine, epoch, authorized>>

\* Coarse lock: only a currently-authorized, up-to-date bank may take it.
AcquireCoarse(b) ==
    /\ coarse = NoneP
    /\ b \in authorized
    /\ localEpoch[b] = epoch
    /\ coarse' = b
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fine, epoch, localEpoch, authorized>>

\* Fine lock nests inside the coarse lock held by the same bank.
AcquireFine(b) ==
    /\ coarse = b
    /\ fine = NoneP
    /\ fine' = b
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, epoch, localEpoch, authorized>>

ReleaseFine(b) ==
    /\ fine = b
    /\ fine' = NoneP
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, epoch, localEpoch, authorized>>

\* Releasing the batch lock settles the batch and advances the epoch (wrapping,
\* so the release is never blocked by an epoch ceiling).
ReleaseCoarse(b) ==
    /\ coarse = b
    /\ fine = NoneP
    /\ coarse' = NoneP
    /\ epoch' = (epoch + 1) % (MaxEpoch + 1)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fine, localEpoch, authorized>>

\* Compliance revokes or restores authorization, but never mid-hold.
ToggleAuth(b) ==
    /\ b # coarse /\ b # fine
    /\ authorized' = (IF b \in authorized THEN authorized \ {b} ELSE authorized \cup {b})
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, fine, epoch, localEpoch>>

Next ==
    \E b \in Banks :
        \/ Sync(b) \/ AcquireCoarse(b) \/ AcquireFine(b)
        \/ ReleaseFine(b) \/ ReleaseCoarse(b) \/ ToggleAuth(b)

Spec ==
    /\ Init /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ SF_vars(ReleaseCoarse("bA")) /\ WF_vars(ReleaseFine("bA"))
    /\ SF_vars(ReleaseCoarse("bB")) /\ WF_vars(ReleaseFine("bB"))
    /\ SF_vars(ReleaseCoarse("bC")) /\ WF_vars(ReleaseFine("bC"))

\* Safety: whoever holds a lock is authorized and not acting on a stale epoch.
NoStaleOrUnauthorizedHolder ==
    /\ (coarse # NoneP => coarse \in authorized /\ localEpoch[coarse] = epoch)
    /\ (fine # NoneP => fine \in authorized /\ localEpoch[fine] = epoch)

\* Liveness: a bank that seizes the batch lock is never stuck holding it forever.
BatchEventuallyReleases ==
    /\ (coarse = "bA" ~> coarse # "bA")
    /\ (coarse = "bB" ~> coarse # "bB")
    /\ (coarse = "bC" ~> coarse # "bC")

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    MaxEpoch = 2
INVARIANT NoStaleOrUnauthorizedHolder
PROPERTY BatchEventuallyReleases
nl:
A clearinghouse runs an interbank settlement batch for three member banks (bA, bB,
bC) using hierarchical locking: a coarse lock on the whole batch, and a nested fine
lock on the individual leg being posted inside it. A bank may seize the coarse lock
only while it is currently authorized to settle and its locally cached view of the
settlement epoch matches the clearinghouse's current epoch; a bank whose cache has
fallen behind must first sync its local epoch up to the current one before it may
try again. Once a bank holds the coarse lock it may take the nested fine lock to work
its leg, release the fine lock when the leg is posted, and only then release the
coarse lock, which settles the batch and advances the clearinghouse to the next
epoch. Compliance may revoke or restore a bank's authorization to settle, but never
while that bank is currently holding either lock. A bank can be slow -- lagging on
syncing its epoch, or taking its time between acquiring and releasing the fine lock
-- but it never crashes or drops out of the batch entirely, so whatever it starts it
eventually finishes.
Actions: a bank syncs its local epoch to the current one; a bank acquires the coarse
batch lock; a bank acquires the nested fine leg lock; a bank releases the fine lock;
a bank releases the coarse lock, advancing the epoch; compliance toggles a bank's
authorization when that bank holds neither lock.
SAFETY PROPERTY: whichever bank currently holds the coarse lock or the fine lock is
always both authorized to settle and synced to the clearinghouse's current epoch --
no unauthorized or stale bank ever holds a lock.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: every bank that seizes the coarse batch lock eventually releases
it, so the batch is never stuck indefinitely in one bank's hands.

---- MODULE W4Od4m5p0t2 ----
(* Two car-wash bay instances share one rinse-reservoir pool. A bay may     *)
(* activate the shared reservoir only after quorum voting by its sensor    *)
(* controllers, and only while a car is actually waiting in its conveyor   *)
(* queue. Activation is mutually exclusive between the two bays.           *)
(* Deactivation is made weakly fair so the reservoir keeps freeing up.     *)
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS BayA, BayB, Controllers, Quorum, MaxQueue, MaxRinsed

Bays == {BayA, BayB}

VARIABLES active, votes, queueLen, totalRinsed

vars == <<active, votes, queueLen, totalRinsed>>

\* Wraps within a bounded range so completed-rinse bookkeeping stays finite.
NextCount(v) == IF v = MaxRinsed THEN 0 ELSE v + 1

TypeOK ==
    /\ active \in [Bays -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ votes \in [Bays -> SUBSET Controllers]
    /\ queueLen \in [Bays -> 0..MaxQueue]
    /\ totalRinsed \in 0..MaxRinsed

Init ==
    /\ active = [b \in Bays |-> FALSE]
    /\ votes = [b \in Bays |-> {}]
    /\ queueLen = [b \in Bays |-> 0]
    /\ totalRinsed = 0

\* A car arrives onto a bay's conveyor queue.
Arrive(b) ==
    /\ queueLen[b] < MaxQueue
    /\ queueLen' = [queueLen EXCEPT ![b] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<active, votes, totalRinsed>>

CastVote(b, c) ==
    /\ ~active[b]
    /\ c \notin votes[b]
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![b] = @ \cup {c}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<active, queueLen, totalRinsed>>

WithdrawVote(b, c) ==
    /\ c \in votes[b]
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![b] = @ \ {c}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<active, queueLen, totalRinsed>>

\* Activation needs quorum votes, a waiting car, and the reservoir currently
\* idle for both bays -- this is where mutual exclusion of the shared pool
\* on the two independent bay instances is enforced.
Activate(b) ==
    /\ ~active[b]
    /\ Cardinality(votes[b]) >= Quorum
    /\ queueLen[b] > 0
    /\ ~ \E o \in Bays : active[o]
    /\ active' = [active EXCEPT ![b] = TRUE]
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![b] = {}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queueLen, totalRinsed>>

Deactivate(b) ==
    /\ active[b]
    /\ active' = [active EXCEPT ![b] = FALSE]
    /\ queueLen' = [queueLen EXCEPT ![b] = @ - 1]
    /\ totalRinsed' = NextCount(totalRinsed)
    /\ UNCHANGED votes

Next ==
    \E b \in Bays :
        \/ Arrive(b)
        \/ Activate(b)
        \/ Deactivate(b)
        \/ \E c \in Controllers : CastVote(b, c) \/ WithdrawVote(b, c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(Deactivate(BayA)) /\ WF_vars(Deactivate(BayB))

\* Literally the cell's property: the two instances never both hold the pool.
MutualExclusion == \A b1, b2 \in Bays : (b1 # b2) => ~(active[b1] /\ active[b2])

\* The shared reservoir returns to idle infinitely often -- no bay
\* monopolizes it forever once it must eventually deactivate.
ReservoirFreesUp == []<>(\A b \in Bays : ~active[b])

====

CONSTANTS
    BayA = BayA
    BayB = BayB
    Controllers = {c1, c2, c3}
    Quorum = 2
    MaxQueue = 2
    MaxRinsed = 3

SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT MutualExclusion
PROPERTY ReservoirFreesUp
nl:
A car-wash conveyor line runs as two independent instances -- two separate
wash bays -- that share one common pool: a single high-pressure rinse
reservoir whose pump can only serve one bay's spray arms at a time. Cars
arrive on each bay's own conveyor queue independently of the other bay.
Before either bay may switch its spray arms onto the shared reservoir it
must gather quorum voting on the action: a set of sensor controllers
watching that bay's queue and water-pressure gauges must cast enough
yes-votes to reach the required quorum before the bay is allowed to
activate. A controller may cast a vote for its bay, or withdraw a vote it
previously cast if conditions change before the bay acts on it. Once a bay
has reached quorum, has a car actually waiting on its conveyor, and the
reservoir is currently idle, it may activate and start drawing from the
shared reservoir; once that car has finished rinsing, the bay deactivates,
gives the reservoir back up, and the finished car leaves the queue.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the two wash-bay instances are never both actively drawing
from the shared rinse reservoir at the same time; activation by one bay is
mutually exclusive with activation by the other.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: whichever bay is currently active on the shared
reservoir always eventually deactivates and gives it up, so the reservoir
becomes idle again infinitely often instead of being monopolized forever.

---- MODULE W4Od4m7p0t5 ----
(* Car-wash conveyor line: a single drive motor is claimed through a
   compare-and-swap on the control register -- the swap only succeeds
   while the register reads free. A privileged admin override can seize
   the drive unconditionally, preempting whichever clamp holds it, and
   later hands it back. Mutual exclusion of the drive must hold
   throughout, and control must never be held forever. *)
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Carriers, Admin, MaxCycle

VARIABLES holders, waiting, overrideActive, cycle

Vars == <<holders, waiting, overrideActive, cycle>>

TypeOK == /\ holders \subseteq (Carriers \cup {Admin})
          /\ waiting \subseteq Carriers
          /\ overrideActive \in BOOLEAN
          /\ cycle \in 0..MaxCycle

Init == /\ holders = {}
        /\ waiting = {}
        /\ overrideActive = FALSE
        /\ cycle = 0

\* A clamp joins the wait set to request control of the drive.
Request == \E c \in Carriers :
              /\ c \notin waiting
              /\ c \notin holders
              /\ waiting' = waiting \cup {c}
              /\ UNCHANGED <<holders, overrideActive, cycle>>

\* Compare-and-swap: succeeds only while the register reads free.
Acquire == \E c \in Carriers :
              /\ c \in waiting
              /\ holders = {}
              /\ ~overrideActive
              /\ holders' = {c}
              /\ waiting' = waiting \ {c}
              /\ UNCHANGED <<overrideActive, cycle>>

\* A controlling clamp lets go once its car has passed through.
Release == \E c \in Carriers :
              /\ holders = {c}
              /\ holders' = {}
              /\ cycle' = IF cycle < MaxCycle THEN cycle + 1 ELSE cycle
              /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, overrideActive>>

\* The admin's privileged override seizes the drive from anyone.
AdminOverride == /\ ~overrideActive
                  /\ overrideActive' = TRUE
                  /\ holders' = {Admin}
                  /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, cycle>>

\* The admin later hands control back to the pool.
AdminRelease == /\ overrideActive
                 /\ overrideActive' = FALSE
                 /\ holders' = {}
                 /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, cycle>>

Next == \/ Request
        \/ Acquire
        \/ Release
        \/ AdminOverride
        \/ AdminRelease

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_Vars /\ WF_Vars(Release) /\ WF_Vars(AdminRelease)

\* At most one controller of the drive at any time.
MutualExclusion == Cardinality(holders) <= 1

\* Control of the drive is never held forever.
EventuallyRelinquished == holders # {} ~> holders = {}

====

CONSTANTS
  Carriers = {car1, car2}
  Admin = Admin
  MaxCycle = 3

SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT MutualExclusion
PROPERTY EventuallyRelinquished
nl:
A car-wash conveyor line has one drive motor that pulls cars through the
wash, and only one carrier clamp may control it at a time. A clamp
requests control by joining a wait set, then acquires the drive only
through a compare-and-swap on the control register: the swap succeeds
only if the register still shows the drive as free, atomically making
the requesting clamp the sole controller. A privileged admin override
can seize the drive at any moment, even preempting whichever clamp
currently controls it, for an emergency stop, and later releases it back
to the pool. A clamp in control eventually lets go of the drive once its
car has passed through.

SAFETY PROPERTY: At most one clamp or the admin controls the conveyor
drive at any time, so control of the drive is always mutually exclusive.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Whenever the drive is under somebody's control, be it
a clamp or the admin's emergency override, it is eventually relinquished
again, so control of the drive never stays locked away forever.

---- MODULE W4Od6m1p3t5 ----
(* Elevator bank token ring: cars are numbered 1..NumCars in ring order.   *)
(* Only the current token holder may commit a slot claim; an admin can     *)
(* forcibly clear a slot at any time without touching the token. The       *)
(* token's rotation is unconditional and weakly fair, so it always keeps   *)
(* returning home even while the admin intervenes on slot allocations.     *)
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS NumCars, NumSlots, MaxOverrides

Cars == 1..NumCars
Slots == 1..NumSlots
Home == 1

VARIABLES tokenHolder, alloc, requested, adminOverrides

vars == <<tokenHolder, alloc, requested, adminOverrides>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ tokenHolder \in Cars
    /\ alloc \subseteq (Slots \X Cars)
    /\ requested \subseteq Cars
    /\ adminOverrides \in 0..MaxOverrides

Init ==
    /\ tokenHolder = Home
    /\ alloc = {}
    /\ requested = {}
    /\ adminOverrides = 0

\* The token rotates unconditionally; this action is always enabled and
\* is the one made weakly fair, independent of slot contention or admin.
PassToken ==
    /\ tokenHolder' = IF tokenHolder = NumCars THEN 1 ELSE tokenHolder + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<alloc, requested, adminOverrides>>

RequestSlot(c) ==
    /\ c \notin requested
    /\ requested' = requested \cup {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenHolder, alloc, adminOverrides>>

\* Only the current token holder may commit a claim into an allocation.
AllocateSlot(s) ==
    /\ tokenHolder \in requested
    /\ ~ \E c \in Cars : <<s, c>> \in alloc
    /\ alloc' = alloc \cup {<<s, tokenHolder>>}
    /\ requested' = requested \ {tokenHolder}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenHolder, adminOverrides>>

ReleaseSlot(s, c) ==
    /\ <<s, c>> \in alloc
    /\ alloc' = alloc \ {<<s, c>>}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenHolder, requested, adminOverrides>>

\* Admin override bypasses the token entirely to clear a slot.
AdminOverride(s) ==
    /\ adminOverrides < MaxOverrides
    /\ \E c \in Cars : <<s, c>> \in alloc
    /\ alloc' = {p \in alloc : p[1] # s}
    /\ adminOverrides' = adminOverrides + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenHolder, requested>>

Next ==
    \/ PassToken
    \/ \E c \in Cars : RequestSlot(c)
    \/ \E s \in Slots : AllocateSlot(s)
    \/ \E s \in Slots, c \in Cars : ReleaseSlot(s, c)
    \/ \E s \in Slots : AdminOverride(s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(PassToken)

\* Literally the cell's property: no slot is ever double-allocated.
NoDoubleAlloc == \A s \in Slots : Cardinality({c \in Cars : <<s, c>> \in alloc}) <= 1

\* The ring keeps turning: the token returns home infinitely often, even
\* though admin overrides can fire at any point without moving the token.
TokenReturns == []<>(tokenHolder = Home)

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    NumCars = 3
    NumSlots = 2
    MaxOverrides = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT NoDoubleAlloc
PROPERTY TokenReturns
nl:
In an elevator bank in a skyscraper, a fixed ring of service cars shares a
small set of priority-access slots (express-hold permissions that let a car
bypass normal call queueing for a floor). A single physical token circulates
around the ring from car to car in a fixed rotation; while a car holds the
token it is the only car allowed to claim a free priority slot for itself.
A car first registers a request to claim a slot, and then, only while it
holds the token, may commit that request into an actual allocation of a
free slot; a car may also give up a slot it currently holds so another car
can claim it later. Building security also has a privileged admin override:
regardless of which car currently holds the token, the admin console can
forcibly clear the allocation of any priority slot at any time (for example
to respond to a fire-panel alert), without waiting for the token to reach
that car and without disturbing the token's own rotation around the ring.
SAFETY PROPERTY: no priority-access slot is ever allocated to more than one
elevator car at the same time, even when the admin override interrupts the
normal token rotation.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: the token always keeps rotating around the ring, so it
infinitely often returns to its home position on the ring rather than
getting stuck at one car forever.

---- MODULE W4Od7m6p2t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Containers, Cranes, MinCapacity, MaxCapacity, NoContainer

VARIABLES pool, leased, expired, capacity

vars == <<pool, leased, expired, capacity>>

\* Lease-based ownership: a crane holds at most one container at a time.
\* A lease can expire while still held; a separate Reclaim step is what
\* actually returns the container to the pool. Capacity is itself a variable
\* since the yard's operating capacity is adjusted at runtime.

Init ==
  /\ pool = Containers
  /\ leased = [c \in Cranes |-> NoContainer]
  /\ expired = {}
  /\ capacity = MaxCapacity

Acquire(c, k) ==
  /\ leased[c] = NoContainer
  /\ c \notin expired
  /\ k \in pool
  /\ Cardinality({cc \in Cranes : leased[cc] # NoContainer}) < capacity
  /\ pool' = pool \ {k}
  /\ leased' = [leased EXCEPT ![c] = k]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<expired, capacity>>

\* The yard's expiry monitor flags only one overdue lease at a time, so a
\* second lease cannot go stale until the first is reclaimed.
ExpireLease(c) ==
  /\ leased[c] # NoContainer
  /\ expired = {}
  /\ expired' = {c}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, leased, capacity>>

\* Reclaiming is the only action that returns an expired container to the
\* pool -- the liveness property depends on this action recurring.
Reclaim(c) ==
  /\ c \in expired
  /\ pool' = pool \cup {leased[c]}
  /\ leased' = [leased EXCEPT ![c] = NoContainer]
  /\ expired' = expired \ {c}
  /\ UNCHANGED capacity

Release(c) ==
  /\ leased[c] # NoContainer
  /\ c \notin expired
  /\ pool' = pool \cup {leased[c]}
  /\ leased' = [leased EXCEPT ![c] = NoContainer]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<expired, capacity>>

AdjustCapacity ==
  /\ \E newCap \in MinCapacity..MaxCapacity : capacity' = newCap
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, leased, expired>>

ReclaimStep == \E c \in Cranes : Reclaim(c)

Next ==
  \/ \E c \in Cranes, k \in Containers : Acquire(c, k)
  \/ \E c \in Cranes : ExpireLease(c)
  \/ ReclaimStep
  \/ \E c \in Cranes : Release(c)
  \/ AdjustCapacity

\* Fairness on the reclaim step (named, non-quantified) is what guarantees
\* expired leases actually drain instead of piling up forever.
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(ReclaimStep)

\* Conservation: every container is in the pool xor held by exactly one
\* crane -- nothing is ever created or destroyed.
ConservationInvariant ==
  LET Held == {leased[c] : c \in {cc \in Cranes : leased[cc] # NoContainer}}
  IN /\ pool \cup Held = Containers
     /\ pool \cap Held = {}

ExpiredEventuallyClear == (expired # {}) ~> (expired = {})

====

CONSTANTS
  Containers = {k1, k2, k3, k4}
  Cranes = {c1, c2}
  MinCapacity = 1
  MaxCapacity = 3
  NoContainer = NoContainer

SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT ConservationInvariant
PROPERTY ExpiredEventuallyClear
nl:
A container-ship crane yard tracks a fixed set of containers that are either
sitting in the yard pool or currently held by one of the yard's cranes on a
time-bounded lease. A crane acquires a container from the pool only while the
yard's currently-declared operating capacity (the number of bays staffed and
powered right now) has room for one more container in the cranes' hands; that
operating capacity is not fixed, it is raised and lowered at runtime as bays
are brought online or taken offline. A crane's lease can expire while the
crane still holds the container, marking that crane's hold as expired but not
yet returning the container; a separate reclaim step is what actually moves an
expired crane's container back into the yard pool and clears the expiry mark.
The yard's expiry monitor flags only one overdue lease at a time: a second
crane's lease cannot be marked expired until the first expired lease has been
reclaimed. A crane may also voluntarily return its container before the lease
expires.
Every container is always accounted for exactly once, either sitting in the
pool or in the hands of exactly one crane: containers are never duplicated and
never vanish as leases are acquired, expire, and are reclaimed, or as capacity
is adjusted. Actions: a crane acquires an available pooled container within
the current capacity limit, a crane's lease on its held container expires, the
yard reclaims an expired crane's container back into the pool, a crane
voluntarily releases its held container, and an operator adjusts the yard's
current operating capacity up or down within its declared range.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the pool and the set of containers held by cranes always partition the full container set exactly, with no container counted twice and none missing, regardless of how leases expire or capacity is adjusted.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: whenever some crane's lease has expired, the yard eventually reclaims every expired container so that no expired hold is left stranded forever.

---- MODULE W4Od9m5p4t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Controllers, Capacity, Quorum

\* committed: load the grid actually carries. proposalAmt = 0 means no open ballot.
\* votes: controllers who voted yes on the open ballot. crashed: controllers gone silent.
VARIABLES committed, proposalAmt, votes, crashed

vars == <<committed, proposalAmt, votes, crashed>>

Init ==
    /\ committed = 0
    /\ proposalAmt = 0
    /\ votes = {}
    /\ crashed = {}

Propose(amt) ==
    /\ proposalAmt = 0
    /\ amt \in 1..Capacity
    /\ proposalAmt' = amt
    /\ votes' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<committed, crashed>>

ProposeAny == \E amt \in 1..Capacity : Propose(amt)

Vote(c) ==
    /\ proposalAmt > 0
    /\ c \in Controllers \ crashed
    /\ c \notin votes
    /\ votes' = votes \cup {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<committed, proposalAmt, crashed>>

VoteAny == \E c \in Controllers : Vote(c)

\* A quorum of live votes commits the block, but never past rated capacity.
Commit ==
    /\ proposalAmt > 0
    /\ Cardinality(votes) >= Quorum
    /\ committed + proposalAmt <= Capacity
    /\ committed' = committed + proposalAmt
    /\ proposalAmt' = 0
    /\ votes' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED crashed

Shed(amt) ==
    /\ amt \in 1..committed
    /\ committed' = committed - amt
    /\ UNCHANGED <<proposalAmt, votes, crashed>>

ShedAny == \E amt \in 1..Capacity : Shed(amt)

\* A silent crash withdraws any pending vote so it cannot count toward quorum.
Crash(c) ==
    /\ c \in Controllers \ crashed
    /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {c}
    /\ votes' = votes \ {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<committed, proposalAmt>>

CrashAny == \E c \in Controllers : Crash(c)

\* A ballot that can never reach quorum (or simply times out) can be withdrawn.
Cancel ==
    /\ proposalAmt > 0
    /\ proposalAmt' = 0
    /\ votes' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<committed, crashed>>

Next == ProposeAny \/ VoteAny \/ Commit \/ ShedAny \/ CrashAny \/ Cancel

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

CapacityNeverExceeded == committed <= Capacity

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Controllers = {c1, c2, c3}
    Capacity = 5
    Quorum = 2

INVARIANT CapacityNeverExceeded
nl:
A regional power grid runs a load shedder that decides, block by block, how much
extra demand the grid may carry. The shedder is not a single trusted authority:
every change to committed load must be approved by a quorum of independent grid
controllers before it takes effect, so no single controller can silently push
the grid over its rated capacity. A controller proposes adding a block of load,
the other controllers cast yes-votes on that specific proposal, and only once a
quorum of votes has been collected does the shedder actually commit the load
increase, and even then only if committed load plus the proposed block still
fits under the grid's rated capacity. Shedding load back off (an emergency
reduction) needs no vote and can happen at any time, since removing load can
never push the grid over capacity. Controllers are not perfectly reliable: any
one controller can crash silently, at which point it simply stops casting
votes and any of its pending, uncommitted votes are withdrawn, rather than
letting a stale yes-vote linger and count toward a quorum it never really
reached. The full action set is: Propose (a controller proposes adding a block
of load, opening a fresh ballot with no votes yet), Vote (a live, non-crashed
controller casts a yes-vote on the open ballot), Commit (once a quorum of
yes-votes is reached, the shedder commits the block, but only if doing so
keeps committed load at or under capacity), Shed (committed load is reduced by
some amount, always permitted), Crash (a controller crashes silently,
joining the crashed set and losing any vote it had cast on the open ballot),
and Cancel (an open ballot that is stalling, for instance because too many
controllers have crashed to ever reach quorum, is withdrawn and its votes
discarded, freeing the shedder to open a fresh proposal).

SAFETY PROPERTY: The load the grid has actually committed never exceeds the
grid's rated capacity, no matter how controllers vote, propose, shed load, or
crash silently.
